title: No Singles Player. No Sania. But India Isn't Invisible at Wimbledon 2026.
excerpt: Five doubles players and two junior prodigies carry the flag at SW19 — while the gap in India's singles pipeline only grows wider.
body:
The Championships opened on Monday at the All England Club, with Jannik Sinner surviving a five-set test against Miomir Kecmanovic and Novak Djokovic rolling past Yibing Wu in four sets. Serena Williams returned as an unseeded wildcard to roaring ovations. The grass courts hummed with the same electricity they always do in late June.

India was there too — just not where you might hope to find it.

For yet another year, no Indian player appears in either the men's or women's singles main draw at Wimbledon. India has not had a genuine singles contender at SW19 since Sumit Nagal's last appearance in qualifying rounds, and the pipeline behind him has produced no one close to cracking the top 100. In a country of 1.4 billion people with a deep appetite for sport, the absence is glaring.

## The Doubles Brigade


![All England Club — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/1/1e/All_England_Lawn_Tennis_and_Croquet_Club_logo.jpg)


What India does have, and in decent numbers, is doubles talent. Five Indian men are in the main draw: **Yuki Bhambri**, who reached a career-high ATP doubles ranking of world No. 18 in February 2026, leads the contingent. **Sriram Balaji**, **Anirudh Chandrasekar**, **Rithvik Choudary Bollipalli**, and **Niki Kaliyanda Poonacha** round out a group that has built credible careers on the Challenger and ATP doubles circuits.



> **"In a country of 1.4 billion people with a deep appetite for sport, the absence is glaring."**


Bhambri, now 34, was once India's great singles hope — a former junior Australian Open champion who fought his way into the top 100 before injuries intervened. His reinvention as a doubles specialist has been quietly successful. He has won multiple ATP doubles titles and is India's highest-ranked player at the tournament.

There are no Indian women in any draw at Wimbledon 2026 — singles, doubles, or mixed — a first in recent memory, and a stark reminder of the void left by **Sania Mirza's** retirement. Mixed doubles pairings will be announced later in the fortnight.

## The Juniors: India's Longer Bet


![Jannik Sinner — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/64/Jannik_Sinner_2025_US_Open.jpg)


Two teenagers carry India's flag in the junior draw. **Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi** competes in girls' singles, and **Arnav Paparkar** in boys' singles, both earning their places through strong runs on the ITF junior circuit this season.

Junior Grand Slams have historically been a launchpad — Carlos Alcaraz and Iga Swiatek both cut their teeth in junior majors. Whether Revathi and Paparkar can translate promise into professional success is the question that hangs over Indian tennis development every generation. The junior pathway in India remains underfunded relative to cricket, and coaching infrastructure outside a handful of academies is thin.

## A Legacy That Demands More

India's Wimbledon history is not one of absence. It is one of brilliance, albeit in doubles. **Leander Paes** won the men's doubles title in 1999 alongside **Mahesh Bhupathi** — a partnership that remains the only all-Indian pairing to win a Grand Slam doubles title. Paes later added four mixed doubles titles at Wimbledon (1999, 2003, 2010, 2015). Bhupathi won two mixed doubles crowns of his own (2002, 2005). Mirza captured the women's doubles title in 2015.


![Miomir Kecmanovic — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/0e/Kecmanovic_RG21_%2811%29_%2851377164760%29.jpg)


No Indian has ever won the Wimbledon singles title.

The distance between those doubles glories and India's present singles drought is not merely about talent. It reflects a structural problem: the All India Tennis Association has struggled to build a sustainable player development programme, top-level coaching remains scarce and expensive, and the financial incentives of cricket continue to pull athletically gifted young Indians toward the bat and ball rather than the racket.

## How to Watch

For NRIs in the United States, Wimbledon 2026 is available on **ESPN** and **ABC**, with every court streamed live on **ESPN+** from 6 a.m. ET daily through the fortnight. In India, coverage is on **Star Sports Network** and streaming on **JioHotstar**. The tournament runs through July 12, with the women's final on July 11 and the men's final on July 12.

Indian tennis fans have plenty to watch this fortnight — Sinner's defence of his title, Djokovic's pursuit of another record, Williams's fairytale return. They just won't be watching an Indian in singles. And that, more than any individual result, is the story that needs telling.
